# Pull Names, Emails, and Phone Numbers Out of Messy Text with Cohere

> **In short:** Cohere's Command model can read a messy block of text and pull out every name, email, and phone number as a clean list. Sign up free, paste your text into the Playground, and ask for structured output. The model can miss details, so always review.

If you've ever stared at a forwarded "who's coming Friday" email, trying to copy ten contact details one by one, this workflow is for you. Cohere is an AI company whose Command model is very good at reading tangled text and pulling structured data out of it. By the end, you'll have a five-minute routine that turns a paragraph of mixed-up contact info into a tidy list you can paste straight into a spreadsheet.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account. Sign-up needs an email address and is available on cohere.com. The free trial comes with enough credits to run this workflow many times.
- A block of messy text with at least five contacts. Good sources: a forwarded meeting email, a pasted conference attendee list, or a paragraph of email signatures from a recent thread.
- A web browser on a laptop or desktop. The Playground is much easier to use on a larger screen than on a phone.
- About 10 minutes of unhurried time.

## Step 1 — Create your Cohere account
Open cohere.com in your browser and look for a "Sign Up" or "Get Started" button — usually in the top-right corner. Click it and register with your email address, or pick Google or GitHub sign-in if those options are visible. After you confirm your email, Cohere drops you on a dashboard. This is your control center: it shows your credit balance, your API keys (those are the codes developers use to call Cohere from their own software — you can ignore them for this task), and links to the tools. If you already have an account, just sign in. If you see a "Tell us about yourself" survey, click the small "Skip" link at the bottom to bypass it.

If your home screen shows "API Keys" or "Billing" instead of a welcome page, you're in the right place — use the left sidebar to find the rest of the tools.

You'll know it worked when you land on a page that shows your name in the top-right corner and a sidebar with at least one tool link.
